title: Incorrect auto-envvar trigger for empty envvar
detail: Using `not envvar` treats empty strings or empty sequences as false and triggers auto-envvar logic, which should only happen when `envvar` is None. This causes an unintended environment variable to be suggested.
note: About the auto-envvar assignment above the planted line; the PR's own logic.

title: Incorrect header name handling
detail: The loop incorrectly sets any header that is not 'Content-Type' to the literal name 'Content-Type', overwriting the original header name and causing all custom headers to be sent as 'Content-Type'. This breaks callers that rely on custom header names.
note: Describes the planted flip: every other header is renamed to Content-Type.

title: Incorrect generator consumption in __exit__
detail: When the context exits normally (typ is None), the code iterates over the generator and immediately raises RuntimeError inside the loop. This causes the context manager to raise an exception instead of simply consuming the generator and returning False, breaking the expected behavior of contextlib._GeneratorContextManager.

title: Incorrect exception raised during generator exit
detail: During the __exit__ path when typ is None, the code iterates over the generator and raises RuntimeError("generator didn't stop") on the first iteration. This incorrectly signals an error for a normal generator that has already yielded and is now exhausted. The intended behavior is to close the generator and return False, suppressing no exception.

title: Missing await on stream.read() in async server
detail: The code calls stream.read() synchronously inside an async function, which returns a coroutine that is never awaited, so the body is never actually read.

title: Missing await on self._reset() in async server
detail: The code calls self._reset() without awaiting it, so the coroutine is never executed and the parser is not reset.

title: Incorrect logic in _starts_statement
detail: The function incorrectly returns True when the leaf has a previous sibling, meaning it is not the first leaf of a statement. This inverted logic causes consecutive `# fmt: skip` statements to be misidentified, leading to a crash.
note: Describes the planted `return True`, but anchored on the function's first line, 12 lines above it, so it isn't counted as found.
